SRC-189:R001.text: ADMISSION BEFORE HANDOFF: before executable Work is handed to an executor SAIPEN mechanically proves EXECUTOR_CAPABILITIES contains REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES; an incompatible executor never receives the Work, and the model is never relied on to discover missing tools after the handoff.
SRC-189:R001.verification: the reference controller admits every candidate through the iteration verdict before it is selected and an executor that lacks a required capability is never selected (test_failover_reaches_a_compatible_executor_without_the_operator); the native host controllers are other repositories and are owed under T-1664

SRC-189:R002.text: CAPABILITY INVENTORY: the executor inventory distinguishes at least shell or process execution, filesystem read, filesystem write, code editing or patch application, recursive repository inspection, Git read, Git write, compiler or build execution, test execution, Windows-native process execution, GUI or computer use, browser or web, SAIPEN control-plane invocation, file upload, download or materialization, and image or visual inspection; exact names are implementation-owned.
SRC-189:R002.verification: test_t1663_ticket_requires InventoryTests: every inventory class the source lists has one distinct name in iteration_verdict.CAPABILITY_INVENTORY, and an inventory requirement is met by the executor that advertises it; regression pair verifier e571ea0713fb70be; core-unit d1fdfeb92c691189

SRC-189:R003.text: PHASE REQUIREMENTS: canonical minimum capability requirements exist per SAIPEN phase. SCOUT: repository and file read, current Work and context access, canonical continuation and control access. BUILD: repository read, repository write or edit, execution when implementation verification requires it. VERIFY: test, build or process execution appropriate to the project, repository read, exact evidence production. REVIEW: repository read, validation and evidence access, execution where the review contract requires dynamic checks. SHIP: canonical control access, required validation and evidence access, release actions only when explicitly authorized. Richer repository contracts are not replaced by these examples.
SRC-189:R003.verification: required_for_state takes the phase: SCOUT requires reading and control, VERIFY and REVIEW also process execution, BUILD, SHIP and any unnamed phase the whole set (test_each_phase_is_charged_for_what_it_executes)

SRC-189:R004.text: TICKET-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS: phase capability is only the minimum and a ticket may require more (C# source modification needs filesystem write, C# build and test execution; a Windows ACL or runtime repair needs Windows-native execution and the privileged broker route; GUI acceptance needs GUI capability or an explicit operator acceptance boundary; browser integration needs browser interaction; an image or layout defect needs visual inspection). Required capabilities are derived from the phase contract, the project manifest and runtime knowledge, ticket metadata, the validation contract and explicit Work requirements; the model is not asked to infer after admission whether it has enough tools.
SRC-189:R004.verification: the required set is the phase contract plus STATE requires plus the claimed ticket's requires field (explicit Work requirements, scoped per phase); test_t1663_ticket_requires GuiAcceptanceTicketTests and InventoryTests; nothing asks the model after admission; regression pair verifier e571ea0713fb70be; core-unit d1fdfeb92c691189

SRC-189:R005.text: CONTROL-PLANE ACCESS: an active SAIPEN operational run requires a canonical route to saipen continue --json or an equivalent trusted control-plane API; an executor that cannot run the CLI directly is acceptable when another trusted control-plane transport is available; with no canonical control-plane route the executor is incompatible with autonomous SAIPEN Work and is not admitted and then told to work manually.
SRC-189:R005.verification: saipen_control is a capability of its own, required in every phase, granted by anything that runs a process or by a named control transport that is not a shell; an executor with the filesystem and no control route is rejected even to read (ControlPlaneTests)

SRC-189:R006.text: NO PROTOCOL BYPASS: an executor that lacks required capabilities does not compensate by editing BOARD or STATE by hand, fabricating LOG events, implementing code without tests when tests are required, reporting completion from static reasoning only, bypassing the lifecycle, or asking the operator to reinterpret the Work as a documentation-only task; the correct action is executor failover.
SRC-189:R006.verification: an executor that lacks a required capability is rejected before it holds the Work, so it has no turn in which to compensate; the listed compensations are refused by their own owners (protected canonical namespace, regression oracle, final-response classes), which this ticket did not change

SRC-189:R007.text: FAILOVER CONTRACT: an incompatible executor is rejected before Work handoff; the current ticket, phase, execution_intent and Work ownership are preserved; the next compatible executor from the configured pool is selected, receives the same canonical Work and continues automatically; autonomous handback and retry counters are not incremented as though the Work had failed, because this is executor admission failure and not project execution failure.
SRC-189:R007.verification: the verdict is read-only: ticket, phase, execution_intent and ownership are unchanged after a rejection (project memory byte-identical), the next compatible candidate of the pool is selected for the same Work, and a mismatch is routing telemetry with no counter (DeadOnArrivalTests)

SRC-189:R008.text: BOUNDED FAILOVER: failover is bounded and deterministic with no infinite provider or model rotation; attempted executors and their rejection reasons are tracked; when at least one compatible executor exists the run continues automatically; when none exists one canonical blocker (NO_COMPATIBLE_EXECUTOR or the repository equivalent) names the missing capability class, the required set and the available pool with what each offers, never a vague message that the agent cannot do this.
SRC-189:R008.verification: a rejected candidate is not tried twice in one capability epoch, and an exhausted pool returns one record: RUNTIME_PAUSED with blocker NO_COMPATIBLE_EXECUTOR, the required set and what each executor of the pool lacked (ExhaustionTests)

SRC-189:R009.text: OPERATOR NOT ASKED TOO EARLY: a missing tool on one executor is not WAIT_USER; before the operator is involved the system tries compatible configured executors, declared provider failover, an available local or native execution path and a canonical broker or control-plane execution path; WAIT_USER is justified only when the configured system has no compatible execution route or a human-owned authorization is required.
SRC-189:R009.verification: a mismatch and an exhausted pool both answer requires_human false; the operator boundary is OPERATOR_WAIT alone, which executor fitness never produces; which further routes a pool contains is the host configuration

SRC-189:R010.text: HANDOFF GENERATION ORDER: no large implementation handoff is generated or sent to an executor before executor admission succeeds; the sequence is resolve Work, derive required capabilities, inspect candidate executor capabilities, admit a compatible executor, generate or attach phase-specific context, execute.

SRC-189:R011.text: MACHINE-READABLE CONTRACT: a canonical machine-readable capability contract carries the required capabilities, the executor capabilities and an admission result with compatible and missing; it is not encoded only in prose instructions; the exact schema is implementation-owned.
SRC-189:R011.verification: the public verdict of saipen iteration carries required_capabilities, executor_capabilities and admission with result, missing and next, for an assessed, an unassessed and an unreadable case (ContractTests)

SRC-189:R012.text: ACTUAL SESSION CAPABILITIES: the capability inventory reflects the tools actually exposed to the current session and never an assumption about a model brand, provider or host application; the same model or provider may run read-only, browser-only, as a full coding environment, in a restricted plugin context or in different hosts.
SRC-189:R012.verification: capabilities are read from the tool map the candidate session advertises; model, provider, route, harness and the other identity keys grant nothing (test_identity_grants_nothing and the T-1619 identity case)

SRC-189:R013.text: RUNTIME DRIFT: capabilities are not persisted forever as static model metadata; they are cached only with freshness or version identity and re-probed when the host, the provider, the session, the tool manifest or the runtime version changes.
SRC-189:R013.verification: nothing about an executor is persisted: admission runs on every switch, negative observations live for one capability epoch and a changed epoch reconsiders (T-1619 epoch cases, run unchanged in this cycle)

SRC-189:R014.text: DEAD-ON-ARRIVAL REGRESSION: a fixture with a SAIPEN-managed C# repository, an active executable ticket in phase BUILD whose validation requires compilation and tests, and an executor exposing only read_tabular and system_todo_write (no shell, file editing, process execution or SAIPEN control route) gives: the executor is rejected before the implementation handoff; no model implementation turn starts on it; the current Work and execution_intent stay intact; no BOARD, STATE or LOG lifecycle mutation is fabricated; compatible executor failover is attempted automatically and the Work continues there when one exists; the operator receives no question; no quota or context is spent on the doomed handoff beyond bounded admission or probe cost.
SRC-189:R014.verification: the fixture is a managed C# project with an active ticket in BUILD and an executor advertising read_tabular and system_todo_write: rejected before selection, Work, intent and project memory unchanged, the compatible candidate selected, requires_human false, and the public command answers the same (DeadOnArrivalTests); the same expectation on the real host is owed under T-1664

SRC-189:R015.text: INVERSE CONTROL: for the same ticket an executor exposing repository read and write, shell or process execution, a SAIPEN control route, C# build and test execution is admitted and receives the Work.
SRC-189:R015.verification: an executor advertising the filesystem and a shell with git and python is admitted in every phase, and the whole filesystem grants patch application as its write half does (InverseControlTests)

SRC-189:R016.text: PARTIAL CAPABILITY CONTROL: an executor with read and write, shell and the SAIPEN CLI but without Windows GUI or computer-use capability is admitted when the current phase requires only implementation and automated tests; when the current acceptance step specifically requires real GUI interaction that step is routed to a capable executor or an operator boundary, or the Work is split by the canonical lifecycle; an executor is never rejected for capabilities the current step does not actually require.
SRC-189:R016.verification: test_t1663_ticket_requires GuiAcceptanceTicketTests: gui@VERIFY admits a GUI-less executor in SCOUT, BUILD and REVIEW and routes VERIFY to a capable one (EXECUTOR_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH, next FAILOVER); regression pair verifier e571ea0713fb70be; core-unit d1fdfeb92c691189

SRC-189:R017.text: READ-ONLY TASK CONTROL: a documentation or read-only audit task stays runnable on a read-only executor when its validation contract requires no writes and no execution; admission is not over-constrained.
SRC-189:R017.verification: test_t1663_ticket_requires ReadOnlyTicketTests: a read_only ticket is admitted on an executor with only filesystem_read and saipen_control in every lifecycle phase; without the field the same executor stops at BUILD; regression pair verifier e571ea0713fb70be; core-unit d1fdfeb92c691189

SRC-189:R018.text: CAPABILITY ESCALATION DURING WORK: when new evidence changes the required capability set during execution (SCOUT reveals that BUILD needs a Windows-native acceptance step) the canonical required capabilities are updated, the current safe step is finished, failover happens at the phase or Work boundary and accumulated evidence and context are preserved; the current incompatible executor is not forced to improvise around missing tools.
SRC-189:R018.verification: test_t1663_ticket_requires EscalationTests: saipen ticket requires raises windows_native@BUILD during SCOUT, the SCOUT step keeps its executor, nothing but the field moves, BUILD fails over; regression pair verifier e571ea0713fb70be; core-unit d1fdfeb92c691189

SRC-189:R019.text: RELATION TO AUTONOMOUS HANDBACK: executor incompatibility feeds the same autonomous continuation machinery as T-1619: INCOMPATIBLE_EXECUTOR leads to failover and continued Work, never to a model final response and operator intervention while another compatible executor exists.
SRC-189:R019.verification: the controller maps EXECUTOR_CAPABILITY_MISMATCH to reroute_executor and never to a stop or a completion (test_failover_reaches_a_compatible_executor_without_the_operator, T-1619 E2E cases)

SRC-189:R020.text: RELATION TO THE QUESTION GATE: an incompatible executor does not ask what it should do instead and does not offer documentation-only mode, manual edits, skipped tests or a protocol bypass; those are not operator decisions while compatible failover remains possible.
SRC-189:R020.verification: an incompatible executor is rejected before a model turn exists on it, so it asks nothing; a handback while executable work remains is classified AUTONOMOUS_HANDBACK by the final-response gate (T-1619 case, run unchanged in this cycle)

SRC-189:R021.text: RELATION TO LAUNCH: the unified launcher and account system exposes executor capability information where relevant; a provider or account that is authenticated and launchable is not thereby an executor capable for this Work: ACCOUNT READY is not EXECUTOR CAPABLE FOR THIS WORK.

SRC-189:R022.text: OBSERVABILITY: a compact diagnostic for executor admission exposes the executor (host, session, capabilities), the Work (ticket, phase, required capabilities) and the admission (result, missing capabilities, next step such as FAILOVER); exact presentation is implementation-owned.
SRC-189:R022.verification: one answer names the executor (id and what it advertised), the Work (ticket, phase, required capabilities) and the admission (result, missing, next), read through bin/saipen iteration --json on a scratch project in VERIFY (review record E-13138)

SRC-189:R023.text: PERFORMANCE: capability admission is cheap and never a full environment audit before every small continuation; it prefers the host tool manifest, a cached session capability fingerprint, bounded lightweight probes and project requirement metadata, with expensive real-process probes only when uncertainty matters.
SRC-189:R023.verification: admission is a comparison of the advertised tool map with a set derived from STATE and the phase; it starts no process and probes nothing (the 22 cases of the module run in under half a second)

SRC-189:R024.text: SECURITY: missing capabilities are never granted by weakening sandbox or security policy and arbitrary shell is not enabled merely because Work requires it; a pre-authorized compatible executor is selected instead; privilege and capability escalation stay policy-controlled; a required capability is not permission to grant that capability.
SRC-189:R024.verification: the admission grants nothing and changes no policy: it compares and returns; an unmet requirement is answered by selecting another executor or by the pause

SRC-189:R025.text: NON-GOALS: forcing every executor to have every tool; disabling read-only agents; bypassing provider sandbox restrictions; granting shell or admin rights automatically; making model self-reported capability authoritative; allowing untested implementation when validation requires tests; turning every capability mismatch into WAIT_USER; provider-specific string matching.
SRC-189:R025.verification: none of the non-goals is produced: a read-only executor is still admitted where reading suffices, identity strings never decide, a mismatch is not an operator wait, and nothing is granted (PhaseRequirementTests, ContractTests)

SRC-189:R026.text: SUCCESS CONDITION: no implementation agent receives Work it is mechanically incapable of executing; for the incident, Work that requires code edit, shell, build and test and SAIPEN control on an executor exposing only read_tabular and a todo tool gives: executor rejected immediately, a compatible executor selected automatically, the same Work continues; never handoff delivered, fourteen seconds of reasoning, a report of no tools and a dead autonomous run.
SRC-189:R026.verification: for the incident shape the executor is rejected at once, the compatible candidate is selected automatically and the same Work continues, shown on the reference controller and the public command; the real host is owed under T-1664

SRC-189:R027.text: INCIDENT AND TEST PERMISSION: the incident executor is SAIOPP from SAIRoute, tried in ZAICODE, a continuation task for a SAIPEN-managed C# project whose executor exposed only read_tabular and system_todo_write and ended after about fourteen seconds; the operator permits testing with that executor as much as needed.
